Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=- 3 \sin{\left(\frac{y}{x} \right)} + \frac{y}{x}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =- 3 \sin{\left(\frac{y}{x} \right)} + \frac{y}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =v - 3 \sin{\left(v \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =v - 3 \sin{\left(v \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- 3 \sin{\left(v \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- 3 \sin{\left(v \right)} \\ \left(- \frac{1}{3 \sin{\left(v \right)}}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{4 x^{3} + x y^{2} - y^{3}}{2 x^{2} y + x y^{2}} + \frac{2 y}{x}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{4 x^{3} + x y^{2} - y^{3}}{2 x^{2} y + x y^{2}} + \frac{2 y}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =2 v + \frac{- v^{3} x^{3} + v^{2} x^{3} + 4 x^{3}}{v^{2} x^{3} + 2 v x^{3}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =2 v + \frac{- v^{3} + v^{2} + 4}{v^{2} + 2 v} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =v + \frac{- v^{3} + v^{2} + 4}{v^{2} + 2 v} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{3 v^{2} + 4}{v^{2} + 2 v} \\ \left(\frac{v^{2} + 2 v}{3 v^{2} + 4}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\sec{\left(\frac{4 x}{y} \right)} - \frac{y}{x}.
$$

If the transformation $y=v(x)x$ is applied to the differential equation, what is the resulting equation?
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the transformation $y=vx$ (where $v=v(x)$), we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x) \\  & =x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given differential equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\sec{\left(\frac{4 x}{y} \right)} - \frac{y}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =- v + \sec{\left(\frac{4}{v} \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =- v + \sec{\left(\frac{4}{v} \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- 2 v + \sec{\left(\frac{4}{v} \right)} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =- 2 v + \sec{\left(\frac{4}{v} \right)} \\ \left(- \frac{1}{2 v - \sec{\left(\frac{4}{v} \right)}}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=e^{\sin{\left(\frac{5 y}{x} \right)}} + \frac{y}{x}.

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =e^{\sin{\left(\frac{5 y}{x} \right)}} + \frac{y}{x} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =v + e^{\sin{\left(5 v \right)}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v & =v + e^{\sin{\left(5 v \right)}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =e^{\sin{\left(5 v \right)}} \\ x\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =e^{\sin{\left(5 v \right)}} \\ \left(e^{- \sin{\left(5 v \right)}}\right)\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{x}.\end{aligned}
